vulnerability.name: CVE-2024-7347
vulnerability.description: ngx_http_mp4_module buffer overread via a specially crafted mp4 file

statements.action_statement: Upstream fix from nginx 1.27.1 / 1.26.2 was backported onto the 1.25.5 source tree before compilation. See build/patches/CVE-2024-7347.patch. The upstream version string is deliberately unchanged at 1.25.5, so version-range matching cannot observe the fix; verify instead with: docker run --rm --entrypoint sh nginx-hardened:1.25.5 -c "grep -c 'unordered mp4 stsc chunks' /usr/sbin/nginx"
statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable arithmetic in ngx_http_mp4_crop_stsc_data is no longer reachable: the chunk-ordering check rejects malformed stsc atoms and the multiplication is widened to 64-bit.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-42767
vulnerability.description: NULL pointer dereference in CRMF EncryptedValue decryption, reachable by an application acting as a CMP client

statements.impact_statement: This OpenSSL is configured with no-cmp, which drops crypto/cmp and crypto/crmf from the build; the CRMF EncryptedValue decryption path the advisory describes is not compiled into the shipped libcrypto.so.3. This is a statement about the artifact, not an argument about reachability, and it is checkable: docker run --rm --entrypoint sh nginx-hardened:1.25.5 -c "grep -ac 'OSSL_CMP\|OSSL_CRMF' /usr/lib/nginx/openssl/lib/libcrypto.so.3" returns 0. build/build.sh asserts the same thing at build time, so the claim cannot quietly become false in a later rebuild. Still reported by scanners because 3.0.21 falls inside the advisory's version range and Debian marks this won't-fix -- which is exactly the gap this document exists to close.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2025-27587
vulnerability.description: Minerva timing side-channel recovering P-384 ECDSA nonces, in OpenSSL's PowerPC-specific code

statements.impact_statement: The advisory is scoped to the PowerPC architecture. This package is built for arm64 (and amd64 on an amd64 host); the ppc64 elliptic-curve implementation the timing leak lives in is selected by OpenSSL's Configure per target and is not compiled here. Checkable against the package's own metadata: docker run --rm --entrypoint dpkg-query nginx-hardened:1.25.5 -W -f='${Architecture}\n' nginx-openssl. Note that unlike CVE-2026-42767 we did not change the build for this one -- there was nothing to remove, because the affected code was never in a non-PowerPC build. Upstream OpenSSL has not shipped a fix in the 3.0 branch, so a version bump cannot clear it either.
